correctness.rationale: For any r>1 a generic point of E_r has exactly four normal feet inside the evolute astroid and two outside, so M(r)=2+2 Area(E_r∩astroid)/(πr). The astroid semiaxes are A=(r²−1)/r and B=r²−1; it lies within E_r exactly through r²≤2, giving 2+3(r²−1)²/(4r²). Beyond, the first-quadrant crossing parameter v=(2r²−1)/(r⁴−1) solves the ellipse–astroid intersection equation, and the two elementary antiderivatives give J and M=2+8J/(πr). Normalized-disk astroid growth proves strict monotonicity. The thin first-quadrant cap has leading horizontal width (2√3/9) ε^(3/2) and height ε(1−z^(2/3)); integrating gives the stated negative 5/2 correction and C²/not-C³ transition. The long-aspect missing quarter cap has leading integral 44√2/15, yielding 4−M~352√2/(15πr³). Independently reconstructed all eight blob identities and their exact assigned Git tree; checked symbolic cap constants, high-aspect integral, and independent ellipse/evolute overlap numerical integrals at multiple aspect ratios. The finite tests corroborate but do not prove the all-parameter analytic deductions.

value.rationale: The area-averaged number of normals is a canonical scale-invariant Santaló-type convex-geometric statistic. Even for ellipses, exact normalization against a four-cusped evolute changes at the nontrivial containment threshold r=sqrt(2). The all-r law, strict monotonicity, and sharp 5/2 and inverse-cubic boundary layers give exact structural and regularity information absent from the classical pointwise normal classification, and a useful benchmark for further convex-body comparisons. It is not just a known pointwise formula reparameterized; genuine integration and asymptotic analysis are required. No claim of general convex-body formula is made.
